Yes, running several coders in T17 is fine, and the plan asks for it. T17's plan entry lets up to four coders read code and judge in parallel. Their results then go to one coder, the applier, which is the only one that edits the source and commits.

What keeps that safe is that only one coder writes to the real files at a time:
- **Judges** only read the code. Each writes its verdicts into its own scratch folder.
- **Recipe testers**, like the one working out the second-try fixes, do their trial edits in private copies of the source tree. They compare the compiler output there, so the real files stay untouched until an applier makes the change.
- **The applier** makes the edits and commits only after the byte-identical rebuild passes.

Right now three coders are listed:
- **A read-only pass over the 466 unplaced uses.** It follows three decisions its expert just gave it.
- **A re-run of the classifier on a snapshot of the tree.** It counts the 9,317 uses already moved as settled, which can settle more of the rest.
- **The recipe coder**, continuing from its progress file.

The trade-off is cost. Parallel coders finish sooner but use more tokens at once. If you'd rather T17 ran fewer at a time, tell me and I'll pass it to the expert.

It will slow T17 down a little, but not much. Most of T17's time goes to the coders thinking and reading code, which uses no CPU on your machine. Your cores matter only in short bursts.

**Right now** WSL sees 16 cores, and the load average is about 2.4. So the three coders running now are using about two cores between them, and the rest sit idle.

**The bursts are where your 95% came from.** Some steps compile all 4,121 source files at once:
- the full byte-identical rebuild (the gate);
- the coders' compiler-output comparisons across every file (about 6 minutes each);
- the signature census.

Those spread across every core they can get, and they're the steps that would have pushed your CPU to 95%.

**What 16 cores changes.** The project's commands already ask for 16 parallel jobs, the gate included (`JOBS=16`), so they fit the limit as is. If WSL had more cores before, those bursts now take longer roughly in proportion. Twice the cores before would mean bursts about twice as long. They're a small part of the total, so I'd expect T17 to finish only a little later overall. Your memory isn't a constraint either: about 25 GB of 31 is free.

**My recommendation: keep the 16-core limit** if it keeps the rest of your PC responsive. Nothing needs changing in the project.
